items.title: through a SUBTRAIT bound, a supertrait method with a DEFAULT runs the default even when the type OVERRIDES it — 0.41.1 prints 'the override' then 'the default'; A142 exposed it (`map_each` took `ListCell`'s lazy default instead of its observer, keeping 92 cells live natively) and `RemoteSource`/`KeyedSource` are exposed the same way (through a subtrait bound they would take the lazy default, not the lease path)
items.discussion: reactive-44 (Order 44); repro `sweeps/order44/reactive-44/finds/subtrait_default_override.vl`; pin `traits::a_supertrait_defaults_override_is_dispatched_through_a_subtrait_bound` (red, `#[ignore]`d on reactive-44); A132 (the leak it re-created); routed around in reactive-44 @c3c644ed
items.body: Dispatch through a subtrait bound must resolve the supertrait member against the receiver's IMPL (override first, default second), as a direct supertrait bound does. Pin both backends; un-ignore the pin; remove `map_each`'s workaround. Sizing S–M; solver, Order 45 FIRST (miscompile).

items.title: `sub` called through an `S: Source` BOUND is emitted as `RemoteSource`'s own INHERENT `sub(\|T\|)` when S is a RemoteSource — the emitter picks the inherent member where the bound asked for the trait's
items.discussion: reactive-44 (Order 44); repro `sweeps/order44/reactive-44/finds/a52_inherent_sub_hijacks_generic_sub.vl`; pin in `markdown.rs` (`#[ignore]`d); B456 door (b) (through a bound the TRAIT answers — the emitter side of that rule); A52
items.body: B456's ranking says the blanket/trait member answers through a bound; the emitter must honour the same rule at the call's mono site. If solver-44's B456 fix already covers it, close on its pin; else Order 45, solver.

items.kind: bug (RUNTIME TypeError — a method table hole)
items.title: a `dyn Source<T>`'s METHOD TABLE has no slot for `Flow::start` (a supertrait/blanket-provided member), so a pipe built over a Source OBJECT fails at run time with a TypeError
items.discussion: reactive-44 (Order 44); repros `sweeps/order44/reactive-44/finds/dyn_source_flow_start.vl`, `dyn_source_pipe_start.vl`; three `dyn_objects` pins `#[ignore]`d; B4 / trait-objects.md §6 (representation); A142 §3.1 (`Source<T> with Flow<T>`)
items.body: The erased pair's table must carry the supertrait's members (and blanket-provided members reachable through the object's trait), or the coercion must refuse a trait whose supertrait members are not in the table. Rec: fill the table (a `dyn Source` IS a Flow). Both backends. Sizing S–M; solver, Order 45 (before A142's `dyn Source` pipes are documented as working).

items.kind: bug (UNCHECKED BOUND — a silent wrong overload)
items.title: a bounded BLANKET impl over `Flow<X>` does not CHECK `X`: a bare `outer.flatten()` on `SignalCell<SignalCell<i32>>` compiles silently as the `Option` join, and sealed it types as the undetermined `MemoCell<Option<U>>` — which is why `std::ui` keeps a `Source` arm beside each `Flow` arm
items.discussion: reactive-44 (Order 44); repros `sweeps/order44/reactive-44/finds/flatten_total_join_bare.vl`, `flatten_over_a_source_of_sources.vl`, `flatten_total_join_annotated.vl`; B299/B305 (blanket subject bounds); A142 §3.2 (`flatten` is the Option join; the total join is `switch(\|inner\| inner)`)
items.body: The blanket's element bound (`Flow<Option<S: Source<U>>>`) must be checked at candidate selection, so a subject whose element is not an `Option` is not a candidate. Pins: the bare total join refused (steer to `switch(|i| i)`), the Option join accepted, the sealed type determined. Then std::ui drops its duplicate `Source` arms. Sizing S–M; solver, Order 45.

items.title: two SAME-NAMED blanket methods over `Flow` subjects with different element bounds (the two `flatten`s) resolve by DECLARATION ORDER, not by which bound holds
items.discussion: reactive-44 (Order 44); B476 (the unchecked bound is why order decides); B456 (the ranking rule, ruled door (b) for concrete-vs-blanket); A86
items.body: With B476's bound check, exactly one candidate survives and order is irrelevant; if both hold, refuse as ambiguous (A86's rule). Pin both declaration orders. Sizing S (rides B476); solver, Order 45.

items.title: a NAMED FUNCTION is refused at a `context`-typed closure parameter — `root.effect(show)` must be written `root.effect(\|v\| show(v))` now that pipe bodies are `context (owner_scope, ambient_nursery)` closures
items.discussion: reactive-44 (Order 44, A142 S2); repro `sweeps/order44/reactive-44/finds/named_function_at_context_param.vl`; B462 (variants as closures — the same expected-type coercion family); B348
items.body: A named function whose signature matches coerces at a context-typed closure position exactly as at a plain one (the context is the CALLER's to supply). Pin. Sizing S; solver, Order 45.

items.title: a pipe stage's CLOSURE PARAMETER inside a GENERIC body is typed as the trait's unsubstituted `T` (`derive` then `switch` under `S: Flow<X>`)
items.discussion: reactive-44 (Order 44); repro `sweeps/order44/reactive-44/finds/generic_derive_then_switch_closure_param.vl`; pin `traits.rs` ~4609 (`#[ignore]`d on reactive-44); B304/B434 (closure parameters typed from the expected type)

items.title: `switch<U, I: Flow<U>>` does not infer `U` when the selector returns a `dyn Flow<i32>` ('cannot infer U') — the mixed-arm selector only compiles with its type arguments written out
items.discussion: reactive-44 (Order 44); repro `sweeps/order44/reactive-44/finds/switch_u_not_bound_through_dyn_flow.vl`; B470 (the per-arm erasure that made the shape compile at all); B412/B430 (dyn at generic positions)
items.body: A `dyn Flow<i32>` at an `I: Flow<U>` position binds `U = i32` from the object's trait arguments. Pin the mixed-arm selector without written arguments (reactive-44's `a142_a_mixed_arm_selector_erases_a_pipe_and_a_root_into_one_flow_object`, un-ignored). Sizing S; solver, Order 45.

items.title: a spawn inside a USER-WRITTEN `context ambient_nursery` closure is NOT registered with the injected nursery: A142 S2's per-run task is cancelled with the run but UNOWNED, so its AbortError is reported on stderr instead of being absorbed
items.discussion: reactive-44 (Order 44, S2); repro `sweeps/order44/reactive-44/finds/spawn_in_injected_nursery_closure.vl`; pin `lifetimes.rs a142_s2_a_cancelled_runs_task_is_owned_and_reports_nothing` (`#[ignore]`d); task.vl (nurseries), destruction.md §9 (`OwnedNursery`)
items.body: A spawn under a closure typed `context ambient_nursery` registers with the nursery the CALLER injected, as a spawn under `nursery(..)`'s body does. Then S2's cancelled tasks report nothing; un-ignore the pin. Sizing S; std/task + the context pass, Order 45.

items.body: Create the run's nursery on the first spawn; pin a task-free run allocates nothing (extend the `quiet`/`busy` pin). Sizing S; std/reactive, Order 45 (with J7).
